title: Foot care for children and teenagers
publisher: Rotherham Doncaster and South Humber NHS Foundation Trust (RDaSH)
claims: Black toenails are caused by injury, which may be one direct injury from dropping an object, but can also occur from badly fitting footwear.
The discolouration is caused by a bleed under the toenail.
Open-toed footwear may be more comfortable, and avoidance of sports is recommended until the pain in the toe subsides.
The nail may loosen and possibly fall off; a new nail will eventually grow back, which can take up to a year for a big toenail.
A new nail can sometimes grow back permanently damaged or thickened.
Trim toenails after a bath or shower, using clippers to cut straight across, leaving a bit of the white part and avoiding cutting too short.
Shoes should have room to wiggle the toes, but shoes that are too big can cause as much trouble as shoes that are too small.
It is advisable to see an HCPC-registered podiatrist if you are worried about a black toenail.
